evidence.claim: There is a possible ambiguity or inconsistency about whether disk quantities (e.g. mass, surface density) are defined in the source frame or the redshifted frame.
evidence.excerpt: The disk is a source-frame physical environment, while the observed GW waveform uses redshifted masses and frequencies. ...I cannot determine from the paper whether the authors have intentionally absorbed all redshift effects into M_z, or whether source-frame and detector-frame quantities have been mixed.

judge_panel.reason: The paper uses M_z as the redshifted mass in GW equations (Eq. 1-2) but uses it also in disk quantities like Σ_0 (Eq. 4) and r_s without clearly distinguishing source-frame disk physics from detector-frame GW quantities. The paper does not explicitly address whether source-frame vs. redshifted-frame quantities have been consistently handled for disk parameters.

The paper defines the system with a "total redshifted mass Mz" and then uses that same quantity in disk/environment formulas, e.g. "rs ≡ 2GMz/c2" in the surface-density expression and "M˙Edd = Mz/50 Myr" in the footnote. Because the paper never explicitly explains whether all disk quantities are intentionally written in the redshifted frame, the source-frame vs detector-frame treatment is unclear from the text alone.

The paper explicitly mixes frames by plugging the redshifted mass into physical disk equations, for instance defining the source-frame scale as "r_s ≡ 2GM_z/c^2" (Eq. 4) and stating they consider an EMRI with "total redshifted mass M_z ... embedded in a thin accretion disk" (Section 3).
